svg.text: flatten-the-cube-to-a-dot: interaction mockup (W-2042). Sketch fidelity; spec: company/design/specs/flatten-the-cube-to-a-dot.md
1. Slice, at predict (locked)
all controls disabled; no change line
2. Slice a corner (slice.done)
new corner, edges, face in warn; trace 1 shows
3. Take the top off (flatten.done)
after the 700 ms lift and stretch; tile = top face
4. Remove an edge, press 1 (shrink.region)
a side region opens to the outside
5. Press 3: first corner (shrink.corner)
a loose end goes with its edge
6. Remove the rest, end (shrink.dot)
one dot, tile beside it, all 12 cells read 1
7. Reveal open, 390 × 844, light (layout estimate)
estimate only: builder measures with tools/reveal-fit.mjs
Flatten the cube to a dot
Corners minus edges plus faces is 2 for a cube.
Three moves show why it is always 2.
Your prediction held / Not quite
Slicing kept the total at 2. Then you took
the top face off, flattened the cube and got
1. Each edge you removed took a region or a
corner with it, so the total never moved,
down to a single dot: 1. Put the top face
back: 2. Any convex solid can be flattened
and shrunk the same way, so corners − edges
+ faces is always 2. This is Euler's
formula.
estimated content bottom 753 px of 844
8. Desktop, 1280 wide: card column 440 px, picture capped at 340 px (light)
same DOM and order; nothing moves beside the picture, so one representation holds
9. Remove the rest after 1 press: playback, 220 ms a removal (reduced motion: the end at once)
